description: We are a team of Computer Engineering students from SSIT (GTU) participating under the Ahmedabad local hub. Our background includes full-stack Python development, machine learning pipelines, data visualization, and software architecture. We are building a scalable, end-to-end solution for our selected NASA challenge.
summary:
**FIRECHRONOS** is a multi-sensor fire intelligence platform designed to harmonize and analyze active fire observations across Asia. It combines NASA FIRMS data from three satellite streams: MODIS, VIIRS NOAA-20, and VIIRS NOAA-21.

The platform addresses the challenge of differences in satellite resolution and detection characteristics by processing observations into a common geographic grid and generating a Harmonized Activity Index (HAI). It transforms raw satellite data into meaningful insights through an interactive Burning Activity Calendar, pan-Asian fire maps, historical trend analysis, sensor comparison tools, and a machine-learning-based seven-day fire activity forecast.

FIRECHRONOS is important because raw satellite observations can be difficult to compare and interpret consistently. By bringing multiple data sources together in one platform, it aims to help researchers, environmental analysts, land managers, and emergency planners better understand fire patterns, identify unusual activity, and support more informed decisions.
details:
FIRECHRONOS – Multi-Sensor Fire Intelligence and Forecasting Platform

1. What does FIRECHRONOS do?

FIRECHRONOS is a web-based, multi-sensor fire intelligence platform that combines satellite fire observations to help users understand, analyze, and anticipate fire activity across Asia.

It uses three NASA FIRMS satellite data streams:

  • MODIS: Observations from the Terra and Aqua satellites.
  • VIIRS NOAA-20: Higher-resolution fire observations.
  • VIIRS NOAA-21: Additional high-resolution observations.

These sensors have different spatial resolutions and detection characteristics. Therefore, their raw hotspot counts cannot always be compared directly. FIRECHRONOS addresses this issue through a harmonization pipeline that processes observations onto a common 0.1° × 0.1° geographic grid and generates a project-specific Harmonized Activity Index (HAI). This creates a more consistent basis for analyzing fire activity across different sensors.

2. How does it work?

The platform follows a data-to-intelligence workflow:

  1. Data collection: Retrieves active fire observations from NASA FIRMS datasets for MODIS and VIIRS NOAA-20 and NOAA-21.
  2. Data processing: Cleans, organizes, and processes satellite observations using a Python-based ETL pipeline.
  3. Sensor harmonization: Converts observations into a common geographic framework and applies calibration methods to account for differences between sensors.
  4. Activity analysis: Calculates HAI to represent harmonized burning activity and identifies unusual activity using statistical anomaly detection.
  5. Machine learning: Uses a dual-head machine-learning approach. The classification component identifies elevated fire conditions, while the regression component forecasts future HAI values for the next 1, 3, and 7 days.
  6. Visualization: Presents the results through interactive maps, calendars, charts, historical trends, and comparison tools.

3. Main features

  • Harmonized Burning Activity Calendar: Explore historical fire activity by date and examine unusual activity.
  • Seven-Day AI Forecast: View predicted future fire activity and categorized risk levels.
  • Pan-Asian Fire Intelligence Map: Explore geographic fire patterns, regional hotspots, and selected fire-prone corridors.
  • Sensor Comparison Lab: Compare MODIS and VIIRS observations to understand differences between satellite data streams.
  • Historical Trend Analysis: Study seasonal patterns and compare activity against historical baselines.
  • Scientific Data Center: Access processed datasets and supporting scientific information for further analysis.

4. Benefits and intended impact

FIRECHRONOS transforms separate satellite observations into a unified analytical platform. Its main benefits include:

  • Making multi-sensor fire observations easier to compare and interpret.
  • Helping users identify unusual fire activity and historical patterns.
  • Providing short-term forecasts to support situational awareness.
  • Enabling regional analysis across national boundaries.
  • Supporting researchers and environmental analysts with accessible visualizations and processed data.

Our intended impact is to support better understanding of fire behavior and provide useful information for researchers, environmental organizations, land managers, and emergency-planning teams. FIRECHRONOS is an analytical and decision-support platform, not a replacement for official emergency alerts or ground verification.

5. Tools and technologies used

Frontend

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS 4
  • Leaflet for interactive geographic maps

Backend and data processing

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pandas and NumPy
  • Scikit-learn and gradient-boosting machine-learning methods

Data and infrastructure

  • NASA FIRMS satellite fire observations
  • MODIS and VIIRS datasets
  • Geographic grid-based data processing
  • Machine-learning models for classification and regression

6. What makes FIRECHRONOS creative and unique?

The main creative aspect of FIRECHRONOS is that it does not simply display satellite hotspots. It first addresses the differences between multiple satellite sensors and then uses the harmonized observations for further analysis.

Instead of treating each satellite dataset independently, FIRECHRONOS combines three observation streams into a common analytical framework. It brings historical analysis, geographic exploration, sensor comparison, anomaly detection, and machine-learning-based forecasting together in one platform.

This combination makes it more than a conventional hotspot visualization dashboard: it is designed to turn satellite observations into interpretable fire intelligence.

7. Factors considered during development

Our team considered:

  • Differences in satellite resolution and detection characteristics.
  • Consistency and reliability of the input datasets.
  • Geographic coverage and regional variations across Asia.
  • Historical seasonality and changing fire patterns.
  • The risk of misleading forecasts and the need to communicate uncertainty.
  • Usability, visual clarity, and accessibility of scientific information.
  • The importance of making the platform useful for both technical and non-technical users.

Overall, FIRECHRONOS aims to bridge the gap between raw satellite fire observations and actionable analytical insights through multi-sensor harmonization, geographic intelligence, and machine-learning-based forecasting.
